rejected.label: contented
rejected.reason: The description portrays a steady, continuing way of living through ordinary days and a settled view of one's life, but it does not explicitly say the state recurs or comes easily, so it reads as an ongoing condition rather than a proneness.
rejected.gloss: This means going through ordinary days at ease with what one has, taking small pleasures without restless wanting, and speaking of one's life with quiet satisfaction.

rejected.label: rueful
rejected.reason: The description characterizes a manner of reflecting and admitting regrets but never says the person does so repeatedly, habitually, or over an extended period, so nothing marks it as recurrent or lasting.
rejected.gloss: This means reflecting with a wry, self-deprecating regret on one's own mistakes and lost chances, smiling ruefully at them and admitting them openly in conversation.

role.label: fugitive
role.gloss: This means living on the run for months, moving between hiding places, using false names, avoiding anyone who might recognize you, and speaking guardedly while watching every stranger who looks your way.
role.reason: Being on the run usually lasts months and rules out most ordinary work, shaping the whole persona.

role.label: housebound
role.gloss: This means being unable to leave home for years, days shaped by what can be done indoors: receiving visitors, managing care from the house, and talking mostly about the window and the world seen from afar.
role.reason: Illness, disability or frailty that keeps someone home can last years and rules out most work, shaping the whole persona.

role.label: ostracized
role.gloss: This means being shunned by the community one lives in: neighbors cross the street, invitations stop, and one's days are spent at the edges of everyone else's company.
role.reason: Exclusion by a community can last months or years and shapes one's whole daily life. It is an imposed low standing that rules out most ordinary roles, so it works as an organizing identity.

lasting.label: beholden
lasting.gloss: This means carrying a debt of gratitude to someone who helped, measuring one's choices against that obligation, and deferring to their wishes while it lasts.
lasting.reason: Owing gratitude or a favor to someone can last months or years, but it is a situational obligation that rules out no profession, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: declining
lasting.gloss: This means living with failing health or strength year after year: needing more help with ordinary tasks, tiring quickly, and speaking often of what the body can no longer do.
lasting.reason: Failing health or strength usually worsens over months or years, so the state lasts long. It is a bodily course no one takes up by temperament and it does not organize a whole identity, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: disabused
lasting.gloss: This means having lost one's old illusions about a person, cause or institution, seeing its faults plainly, and speaking of former hopes with dry, unsentimental clarity.
lasting.reason: Once freed from an illusion, a person keeps seeing things clearly for years. It is a standing outlook that colors the whole life, but it is not a profession or office, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: emigrating
lasting.gloss: This means living between two countries for months, selling possessions, sorting visas and paperwork, and speaking of home in the past tense while still living there.
lasting.reason: The process of leaving one's country permanently usually runs for many months, often longer, with sales, visas and farewells. It is a transition rather than an identity that organizes the whole persona.

lasting.label: expecting
lasting.gloss: This means carrying a child through months of growing bodily change: tiring easily, planning around appointments and due dates, and speaking often of the baby, the nursery and what is coming.
lasting.reason: Pregnancy lasts about nine months, so it is lasting. It rules out no profession, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: heartsick
lasting.gloss: This means grieving a loss month after month, with sadness heavy in every ordinary day: losing interest in company, weeping at small reminders, and speaking of what is gone in a flat, hollow voice.
lasting.reason: Deep grief over a loss can last months, as with bereavement, and it rules out no profession, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: liable
lasting.gloss: This means carrying answerability for a debt or harm over an extended period, with its legal demands and payments hanging over one's finances, and speaking of the matter with wary caution.
lasting.reason: Legal or financial answerability for a debt or harm often runs for months or longer, depending on the claim. It is imposed from outside, so it is not a role or a predisposition.

lasting.label: miserably partnered
lasting.gloss: This means living day after day with a partner one wishes one had not chosen, bickering over small matters, and keeping the household running in cold, strained silence.
lasting.reason: An unhappy marriage or partnership is a standing condition lasting years. It does not rule out professions, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: nascent
lasting.gloss: This means working at the earliest, still-forming stage of some craft or venture, tentatively and unsure of one's footing, building skills and habits that are not yet set.
lasting.reason: An early, still-forming stage of a project or talent can last months, and a person can stay in it for a long while. It is a stage rather than a role, so role is false.

lasting.label: overburdened
lasting.gloss: This means carrying more work and worry than one can manage for months, working late and skipping rest, snapping at small requests, and answering every question with a list of what is already due.
lasting.reason: Excess work or pressure often lasts months, as in a long crunch or overloaded year. It is a condition of circumstances rather than a calling or office, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: pretty well
lasting.gloss: This means getting through ordinary days without serious illness, with an occasional cold or ache, and answering inquiries about one's health with a cheerful report that one is fine.
lasting.reason: Fairly good general health can persist for years in a healthy person, so the state lasts. It is a bodily condition, not a role, and it does not organize an identity.

lasting.label: thriving
lasting.gloss: This means living with good health and steady success, with days full of work and pleasures that come easily, and speaking of one's life with easy confidence and quiet satisfaction.
lasting.reason: Flourishing health and success can last years, but it is a state of circumstance rather than a role or a temperament-based predisposition.

lasting.label: unacknowledged
lasting.gloss: This means working on without credit for one's efforts, watching others take praise for shared work, and speaking with a wry bitterness about being passed over in meetings and reviews.
lasting.reason: Being overlooked for worth or work can last months or years in a workplace, but it is an external circumstance rather than a role or temperament.

lasting.label: unemployed
lasting.gloss: This means having no paid work for month after month, filling empty days with job searches and small economies, and carrying the strain of money worries and lost routine.
lasting.reason: Being out of paid work often lasts months, sometimes years. It does not rule out a profession or organize the whole identity, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: unhealthy
lasting.gloss: This means living with a body that is persistently unwell, managing fatigue, pain and frequent doctor visits, and having daily plans shaped around what one's health allows.
lasting.reason: Poor physical health from chronic illness can last years. It does not organize a whole identity and no temperament brings it about, so it is not a role.

lasting.label: unmastered
lasting.gloss: This means still learning one's craft, practicing with frequent errors, relying on teachers and reference books, and feeling the gap between what one attempts and what one can yet do.
lasting.reason: Not yet skilled at one's craft is a learning stage that often lasts months or years. It is a stage of learning rather than an identity that organizes the whole persona.

lasting.label: unpunished
lasting.gloss: This means carrying on with ordinary work and relationships while a past wrong sits unanswered, knowing that no one will hold one to account and feeling the weight of that freedom in private.
lasting.reason: Having escaped punishment for past wrongs is a standing situation that can persist for years. It is not a profession or rank, so it does not organize the whole persona.

predisposition.label: amorous
predisposition.gloss: This means falling readily into romantic longing and flirtation, noticing attractive people, lingering over touch and glances, and speaking with warmth and suggestion that signals desire.
predisposition.reason: Romantic desire is an emotional state lasting hours or days. Some people are habitually amorous, and the ordinary word is already used for such a person.

predisposition.label: disheveled
predisposition.gloss: This means going about with hair uncombed, shirts untucked and clothes rumpled, seldom checking one's appearance and not minding who notices.
predisposition.reason: Untidy dress or hair is a passing look lasting hours or days. Some people habitually appear this way, and ordinary speakers would say a person is always disheveled.

predisposition.label: fearful
predisposition.gloss: This means expecting danger in ordinary situations, flinching at unfamiliar sounds and strangers, and voicing worries about what might go wrong before it does.
predisposition.reason: Fear is a passing feeling, but some people are habitually fearful, and ordinary speakers already use the word for them.

predisposition.label: inconsolable
predisposition.gloss: This means breaking down over every disappointment or loss and staying inconsolable for long stretches, pushing away the comfort friends offer and insisting nothing they say can help.
predisposition.reason: Acute inconsolable grief lasts hours to days. Some people habitually take losses hard and resist comfort, so the predisposition is plausible and the word already fits.

predisposition.label: lonesome
predisposition.gloss: This means feeling the absence of company keenly and often, drifting into sad thoughts when alone, and wanting contact while finding it hard to ask for it.
predisposition.reason: Loneliness from lacking company usually passes within days, though some people carry it as a standing sadness. A habitual lonesomeness is plausible, and ordinary speakers do say a person is lonesome.

predisposition.label: nervous
predisposition.gloss: This means jumping at sudden noises, rehearsing what could go wrong, fidgeting in new situations, and voicing worries before anything has happened.
predisposition.reason: Anxiety or edginess comes and goes over hours or days. Many people are habitually nervous, and the ordinary word fits.

predisposition.label: remorseful
predisposition.gloss: This means dwelling often on past wrongs one has done, feeling guilt that surfaces readily, and saying sorry in a way that shows the regret is still weighing on one.
predisposition.reason: Guilt over past wrongs typically lasts days to weeks, not months. People who often feel remorse are plainly called remorseful.

predisposition.label: repentant
predisposition.gloss: This means turning back again and again to wrongs one has committed, seeking to make amends, and speaking of them with humility and a readiness to change one's ways.
predisposition.reason: Regret for a wrong usually lasts days to weeks and ends with amends. Habitual repentance is plausible, and the word fits people who repeatedly express it.

predisposition.label: rumpled
predisposition.gloss: This means going about with clothes creased and hair untidy as a matter of course, paying little attention to appearance and seeming unbothered by how one looks to others.
predisposition.reason: Untidy dress and hair is a look of the moment lasting hours. Some people habitually look rumpled, and that word already describes them.

predisposition.label: sulky
predisposition.gloss: This means going quiet and withdrawn after a slight, answering questions in clipped words, avoiding eye contact, and nursing resentment long after the matter has been settled.
predisposition.reason: A sulk lasts hours or a day or two; people who often sulk are commonly called sulky.

predisposition.label: tearful
predisposition.gloss: This means welling up at small kindnesses, sad songs or hard news, speaking with a thickened voice, and reaching for a tissue more often than others would expect.
predisposition.reason: Crying or near tears passes within hours; people who often cry easily are commonly called tearful.

predisposition.label: teasing
predisposition.gloss: This means finding the weak spot in friends' stories and plans and poking at it with a grin, turning remarks into light jabs, and treating mild embarrassment in others as a game worth continuing.
predisposition.reason: Playful mocking is a momentary act within a conversation; some people habitually tease, commonly called teasing.

predisposition.label: thankful
predisposition.gloss: This means noticing small favors and saying thank you readily, pausing to name what others have done, and expressing appreciation in notes, toasts and ordinary conversation.
predisposition.reason: Gratitude is a momentary feeling; people who often feel and express thanks are commonly called thankful.

predisposition.label: unhappy
predisposition.gloss: This means dwelling readily on what is wrong in one's life, complaining about circumstances, and letting a discontented tone color everyday conversation.
predisposition.reason: Feeling sad or discontented passes within hours or days. People who often feel this way are commonly called unhappy, so the name fits.

predisposition.label: woeful
predisposition.gloss: This means slipping readily into deep sorrow, speaking of hard luck and lost hopes in a heavy voice, and carrying a gloom that colors even small events.
predisposition.reason: Deep sorrow lasts hours or days. Some people habitually slip into this sorrowful, heavy manner, and the word already describes such a person.

renamed.label: afraid
renamed.gloss: This means bracing for danger that has not yet arrived, scanning rooms for threats, and hedging every plan with what might go wrong, so that caution shapes what one says and does.
renamed.reason: Fear is a passing emotional state lasting hours. Some people are habitually fearful, so a predisposition is plausible, but ordinary speakers would say 'fearful' rather than 'afraid' for such a person.

renamed.label: agitated
renamed.gloss: This means getting worked up quickly over small irritations and pressures, pacing or fidgeting, speaking faster and more sharply, and struggling to sit still until things settle.
renamed.reason: Emotional disturbance lasts hours or days. Some people are habitually easily worked up, though 'agitated' is not the everyday word for that temperament.

renamed.label: alone
renamed.gloss: This means choosing to spend most free hours without company, turning down invitations for quiet time alone, and speaking of solitude as the place where one thinks and recovers.
renamed.reason: Being without others present is a situational state lasting hours. Some people habitually prefer solitude, a predisposition the ordinary word 'solitary' already names.

renamed.label: bedraggled
renamed.gloss: This means neglecting one's dress and grooming, letting clothes stay rumpled and dirty, hair go unbrushed, and treating tidiness as a bother not worth the effort.
renamed.reason: Wet, dirty, disheveled appearance is a passing condition lasting hours. Some people habitually neglect their dress and grooming, so a predisposition is plausible, though 'bedraggled' is not the everyday word for it.

renamed.label: befogged
renamed.gloss: This means losing the thread of conversations, forgetting appointments and names, and answering questions with muddled, half-finished thoughts because attention keeps drifting elsewhere.
renamed.reason: Muddled thinking is a passing state lasting hours. Some people habitually lose focus and think in a muddle, which the everyday word 'scatterbrained' names better than 'befogged'.

renamed.label: bejeweled
renamed.gloss: This means dressing in heavy, glittering jewelry as a matter of course, drawing attention to one's rings and necklaces, and taking pride in an ornate, showy appearance.
renamed.reason: Wearing heavy jewelry is an outfit worn for a day or an evening. A habitually flashy dresser is plausible, but the word bejeweled does not name that habit.

renamed.label: benumbed
renamed.gloss: This means keeping feelings at a distance, often seeming flat or absent when news lands, and going on with routines without much felt response.
renamed.reason: Shock-induced numbness passes within hours or days. Habitual emotional detachment is a plausible temperament, though no ordinary word for it is benumbed.

renamed.label: bored
renamed.gloss: This means losing interest quickly in whatever is happening, fidgeting through slow stretches, and complaining or changing the subject when a task drags on.
renamed.reason: Boredom is a mood of hours. Some people are routinely bored, and the ordinary phrase for that is easily bored.

renamed.label: clean
renamed.gloss: This means keeping one's body, clothes and surroundings spotless as a matter of routine, washing often, and feeling uneasy around dirt or grime.
renamed.reason: Being washed is a momentary condition. Habitual personal cleanliness is a plausible predisposition, though clean is not the ordinary word for it.

renamed.label: concerned
renamed.gloss: This means fretting over possible problems before they happen, checking on things repeatedly, and voicing worries that others find out of proportion.
renamed.reason: Worry about a particular matter passes within hours or days. A habitually worried temperament is plausible, and the ordinary word for it is anxious.

renamed.label: contrite
renamed.gloss: This means owning mistakes readily, apologizing at once, and carrying guilt for a long time after hurting someone, wanting to make amends.
renamed.reason: Remorse for a wrong usually fades within days or weeks. A habit of readily feeling and voicing guilt is plausible, though contrite is not the ordinary word for it.

renamed.label: cross
renamed.gloss: This means snapping at small irritations, speaking curtly to people who interrupt, and showing displeasure in tone and expression long before anyone has done much wrong.
renamed.reason: Annoyance or anger passes within hours. A habitually irritable temperament is plausible, and the ordinary word for it is irritable, not cross.

renamed.label: delighted
renamed.gloss: This means lighting up at small pleasures, such as a good meal, a kind remark or a bright morning, and saying so with warm, unguarded enthusiasm.
renamed.reason: Delight is a passing mood lasting hours. Some people are readily delighted by small pleasures, but ordinary speakers would not call them delighted, so the name needs replacing.

renamed.label: depressed
renamed.gloss: This means sinking easily into low spirits, seeing little point in plans, and speaking of the day's prospects in flat, heavy terms.
renamed.reason: Current low mood passes in days or weeks. People who often sink into low moods exist, but ordinary speakers would call them gloomy rather than depressed, so the name needs replacing.

renamed.label: desirous
renamed.gloss: This means wanting things intensely and persistently, measuring one's contentment by what one still lacks, and letting envy of others' possessions color one's conversation.
renamed.reason: Strong wanting comes and goes over hours or days. Some people are habitually covetous, and that is the ordinary word for the standing predisposition, so the name needs replacing.

renamed.label: destined
renamed.gloss: This means talking as though one's future is already written, expecting doors to open and greatness to arrive, and brushing aside ordinary limits.
renamed.reason: Being fated for a future is a belief or status held for a while rather than a mood. A habitual sense of being destined for greatness is plausible, and grandiose is the ordinary word for it.

renamed.label: diluted
renamed.gloss: This means holding one's beliefs and commitments loosely, backing away from stated positions, and offering qualified, watered-down enthusiasm for whatever is asked of one.
renamed.reason: Weakened conviction or force is a passing condition lasting weeks at most. Some people habitually hold their convictions loosely, but no ordinary word fits that, so a short phrase is needed.

renamed.label: disgusted
renamed.gloss: This means recoiling readily from crude food, messes or bodily matters, and voicing one's revulsion bluntly while steering away from anything unpleasant.
renamed.reason: Revulsion passes within hours. Some people are habitually squeamish, and that is the ordinary word for a standing predisposition to recoil, so the name needs replacing.

renamed.label: dissatisfied
renamed.gloss: This means finding fault with one's job, home and prospects, measuring every situation against something better, and voicing discontent to anyone who will listen.
renamed.reason: Discontent with circumstances usually lasts days or weeks, but some people habitually find fault with their lives, so a predisposition is plausible.

renamed.label: diverted
renamed.gloss: This means letting attention slide off the task at hand toward whatever passes by, abandoning plans mid-sentence, and rarely finishing what one began.
renamed.reason: Being distracted passes within hours. Some people are habitually pulled off course by whatever passes, so a predisposition is plausible.

renamed.label: embroiled
renamed.gloss: This means picking arguments, taking sides in every dispute among colleagues or family, and carrying grudges forward into the next quarrel.
renamed.reason: Being caught in a dispute usually runs weeks, sometimes longer, but not months as a standing identity. Some people habitually pick quarrels, so a predisposition is plausible.

renamed.label: enervate
renamed.gloss: This means moving slowly through the day with little drive, answering in flat, low-energy tones, and letting tasks sit unfinished for want of the will to start them.
renamed.reason: Being drained of energy lasts hours or days. Some people habitually feel listless and low in vigor, so a predisposition is plausible.

renamed.label: enkindled
renamed.gloss: This means taking fire quickly at new ideas and projects, talking about them with bright energy, and pursuing them with an eagerness that others find infectious.
renamed.reason: Being filled with enthusiasm passes within hours or days. Some people habitually take fire at new ideas, so a predisposition is plausible.

renamed.label: exasperated
renamed.gloss: This means snapping at small delays and mistakes, sighing audibly at repeated requests, and running short of patience with people who keep asking the same things.
renamed.reason: Irritation and being fed up pass within hours or days. Some people are habitually short-tempered and impatient, so a predisposition is plausible.

renamed.label: fasting
renamed.gloss: This means refusing food by deliberate choice on set days, speaking calmly about one's restraint, and turning down meals and treats that others take for granted.
renamed.reason: A fast lasts days at most. Some people habitually fast by choice, and that restraint shows in how they talk about food.

renamed.label: filthy
renamed.gloss: This means letting one's body and clothes go unwashed for days, wearing the same grimy garments, and shrugging off remarks about the smell or the mess.
renamed.reason: Being very dirty passes within hours or days. Some people habitually neglect cleanliness, which shows in their appearance and habits.

renamed.label: flexed
renamed.gloss: This means holding one's shoulders and jaw tight through the day, moving stiffly and quickly, and answering in clipped words as if braced for something.
renamed.reason: Tensed muscles relax within hours. Some people habitually hold their bodies tight, which shows in how they move and speak.

renamed.label: grizzling
renamed.gloss: This means fretting over small discomforts, whining about delays and minor slights, and voicing a steady stream of complaints that others find tiring.
renamed.reason: A fussy, whimpering mood passes within hours. Some people habitually fret and complain, which shows in their speech.

renamed.label: grubby
renamed.gloss: This means going about with unwashed hair, rumpled and grimy clothes, and nails left dirty, showing little concern for how one looks to others.
renamed.reason: Being dirty and unwashed passes within days. Some people habitually neglect their appearance, which shows in how they present themselves.

renamed.label: high
renamed.gloss: This means drinking or using drugs to excess most days, chasing the lift they bring, and letting that habit steer one's money, time and company.
renamed.reason: Intoxication passes within hours. Some people habitually drink or use drugs to excess, which is a vice that shows in their talk and habits.

renamed.label: inspired
renamed.gloss: This means greeting new projects and ideas with eager energy, launching into them with fervor, and talking about them in glowing terms until the enthusiasm spreads to others around.
renamed.reason: Creative inspiration lasts hours or days. Some people are habitually eager and quick to be stirred by new ideas, but 'inspired' is not the everyday word for that, so a different name is needed.

renamed.label: insurrectional
renamed.gloss: This means chafing against authority and rules, siding readily with those who defy the government, and speaking of rising up against unjust power with a fierce, restless anger.
renamed.reason: Taking part in an uprising typically lasts days to weeks and is not a standing condition. A habit of defying authority is plausible, though the word 'insurrectional' is not used for it.

renamed.label: lamenting
renamed.gloss: This means dwelling on losses and disappointments, bemoaning what has gone wrong in a plaintive voice, and returning again and again to what was lost as if the grief were never quite finished.
renamed.reason: Lamenting a loss is an expressive act that typically runs for weeks, not months. A habit of bemoaning losses in a plaintive way is plausible, and 'mournful' is the ordinary word for it.

renamed.label: laughing
renamed.gloss: This means finding humor in almost everything, breaking into laughter at small jokes and mishaps, and filling conversations with teasing remarks and easy giggles.
renamed.reason: Laughing or being amused comes and goes within hours. Some people habitually laugh readily, though 'laughing' itself is not the usual trait word for that.

renamed.label: lecturing
renamed.gloss: This means sliding into sermonizing whenever a topic arises, instructing friends on how they ought to live or think, and answering objections with a patient, superior tone of correction.
renamed.reason: Giving a formal talk lasts an hour or so. A habit of moralizing and instructing others is plausible, and 'preachy' is the ordinary word for it.

renamed.label: low
renamed.gloss: This means slipping easily into dejection, speaking of little that pleases, dragging through ordinary tasks, and answering friends with flat, weary replies.
renamed.reason: Low spirits typically last days or a few weeks and then lift. People are often prone to dejection, but 'low' is not the ordinary trait word for that.

renamed.label: moping
renamed.gloss: This means sinking into gloomy listlessness over small disappointments, sulking when crossed, and answering questions with sighs and sullen short replies.
renamed.reason: A spell of gloom and sulking lasts hours or days. Some people mope habitually, and the ordinary word for that is mopey.

renamed.label: numb
renamed.gloss: This means going flat and far away inside, meeting loss, joy and ordinary news with the same blank, and having to be prompted to say what one feels.
renamed.reason: Emotional numbness after shock usually passes within days. Some people habitually go emotionally flat and detached, so a predisposition is plausible, but the word numb is not what people call such a person.

renamed.label: offline
renamed.gloss: This means keeping phone and laptop switched off for long stretches, answering messages late or not at all, and feeling relieved rather than cut off when unreachable.
renamed.reason: Being unreachable digitally is a passing situation lasting hours or days. Some people habitually disconnect, so a predisposition is plausible, though the word offline does not name that person.

renamed.label: penitent
renamed.gloss: This means dwelling on a past wrong, apologizing repeatedly, and bringing up one's regret unprompted, often making amends and checking whether the hurt person has forgiven.
renamed.reason: Remorse for a past wrong usually fades over weeks, not months. Some people are habitually remorseful and apologize often, a predisposition that the word penitent does not quite name.

renamed.label: played out
renamed.gloss: This means running out of energy well before others do, flagging after modest effort, and speaking of oneself as spent while everyone else is still going.
renamed.reason: Exhaustion from exertion passes within hours or a day. Some people habitually tire quickly, so a predisposition to it is plausible, though the state's own name is not the usual word for it.

renamed.label: prettified
renamed.gloss: This means spending long, unhurried time on hair, clothes and makeup, checking one's reflection often, and remarking on how one looks as if appearance were a daily project.
renamed.reason: Dressing up for an occasion lasts hours. Some people habitually fuss over their appearance, so the predisposition is plausible, though 'prettified' is not a word for such a person.

renamed.label: pulled down
renamed.gloss: This means wearing out quickly under pressure, letting fatigue and setbacks drain one's spirits, and sounding tired and flat when describing even ordinary demands.
renamed.reason: Being worn down in body or spirits typically lasts weeks after strain and then recovers, so it is not lasting. Some people habitually flag under pressure, so the predisposition is plausible.

renamed.label: rattled
renamed.gloss: This means losing composure at the slightest provocation, fumbling words, snapping at others, and reacting to small upsets with visible agitation before slowly regaining control.
renamed.reason: Being emotionally thrown off composure passes within hours. Many people are easily rattled, so the predisposition is plausible and the phrase 'easily rattled' is the ordinary name.

renamed.label: rekindled
renamed.gloss: This means bouncing back quickly after disappointment, reviving hope and enthusiasm for projects that had seemed finished, and talking about new beginnings with real energy.
renamed.reason: Revived hope or enthusiasm is a passing mood lasting hours or days. A person often bouncing back is better named resilient, a plausible habitual predisposition.

renamed.label: rushed
renamed.gloss: This means rushing through tasks and conversations as a habit, speaking quickly, checking the clock often, and feeling impatient whenever one has to wait or slow down.
renamed.reason: Time pressure and hurry pass within hours or days. A person who is always hurried is a plausible temperament, though the word rushed does not name it.

renamed.label: satisfied
renamed.gloss: This means finding contentment easily in one's circumstances and possessions, taking little notice of what is missing, and speaking of what one has with quiet gratitude.
renamed.reason: Contentment passes over hours or days. Some people habitually feel content with what they have, and ordinary speech calls that contented.

renamed.label: scoffing
renamed.gloss: This means greeting other people's earnest plans and claims with a sneer and a mocking remark, treating enthusiasm as naive, and making scornful jokes at others' expense.
renamed.reason: A scornful mood lasts hours. Some people habitually mock and sneer, and 'scornful' is the ordinary word for that person.

renamed.label: snarling
renamed.gloss: This means answering questions and requests with curt, irritable remarks, bristling at small delays or criticism, and letting irritation show in one's tone and manner.
renamed.reason: An angry, hostile mood lasts hours. Some people habitually snap and bristle, and 'snappish' is the ordinary word for that.

renamed.label: sober
renamed.gloss: This means abstaining from alcohol as a settled rule, turning down drinks at gatherings without apology, and keeping a clear head through evenings others spend drinking.
renamed.reason: Not being intoxicated is a momentary condition of hours. Some people habitually abstain from alcohol, which ordinary speech calls teetotal.

renamed.label: sorrowing
renamed.gloss: This means carrying a settled melancholy, dwelling on losses and disappointments, and speaking of hard things in a low, grieved voice as if sadness were the natural tone of life.
renamed.reason: Grief in the moment lasts hours or days. Some people habitually carry a sad, grieving disposition, which ordinary speech calls sorrowful.

renamed.label: stunned
renamed.gloss: This means being knocked silent by news or events that others take in stride, standing motionless for a moment, and then struggling to find words for what just happened.
renamed.reason: Shock or astonishment passes within minutes or hours; some people are easily stunned, but the ordinary word for that is not clearly established.

renamed.label: thinking
renamed.gloss: This means pausing before answering, turning questions over at length, and voicing conclusions only after weighing alternatives, so that others often wait for the thought to finish.
renamed.reason: Being engaged in thought is a momentary activity, not a lasting condition or a predisposition with a common name.

renamed.label: tittering
renamed.gloss: This means breaking into nervous giggles at tense moments, in serious meetings and at awkward silences, and covering one's own discomfort with laughter that others find hard to take seriously.
renamed.reason: Quiet nervous giggling is a momentary reaction; a habitual giggler is not a standard named predisposition here.

renamed.label: torpid
renamed.gloss: This means moving slowly through the day, answering questions after long pauses, and lacking the drive to start tasks, so that others must prod and wait for any response.
